text: The Lal Bahadur Shastri Dam, also known as the Almatti Dam, is a hydroelectric project situated on the Krishna River in North Karnataka, India, completed in July 2005. Its target annual electric output is 560 MU (or GWh). The Almatti Dam serves as the main reservoir for the Upper Krishna Irrigation Project, with a 290 MW power station located on the right side of the dam. This power station consists of five 55 MW generators and one 15 MW generator, all using vertical Kaplan turbines. After power generation, water is released into the Narayanpur reservoir to meet downstream irrigation demands. Two separate power generation facilities—Almatti 1 Powerhouse and Almatti II Powerhouse—are spaced apart and contribute to power production. Initially, the project's estimated cost was ₹1,470 crores, but after the transfer of management to the Karnataka Power Corporation Limited (KPCL), the cost was reduced by over fifty percent to ₹674 crores, with the final completion cost recorded at ₹520 crores. Construction was completed in less than forty months, ending in July 2005. The dam is located on the border of Vijayapura and Bagalkote districts, primarily within Vijayapura district, though significant areas of Bagalkote district were submerged during reservoir filling. It has a gross water storage capacity of 123.08 TMC at 519 meters MSL. The backwaters of the dam support several migratory birds during summer. Originally, the full reservoir level was restricted to 160 feet MSL by the Supreme Court of India, but following the resolution of the Krishna River conflict between Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, and Maharashtra by the Brijesh Kumar Tribunal, the dam was authorized to be raised to 524 feet MSL, providing nearly 200 TMC gross storage capacity. The dam features 26 radial spillway gates.
